extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, and publishers submitting nonfiction business books to the SABEW Best in Business Book Awards
extracted.subtask_short: SABEW Best in Business Book submission
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and eligibility criteria for submitting nonfiction business books to the Society for Advancing Business Editing and Writing (SABEW) Best in Business Book Awards, including category definitions, required materials, formatting, fees, and judge priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timeframe (eligibility window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must be published from August 1, 2024, through July 31, 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the original publication date of the submission and the date the book was published in English. The contest recognizes books published in that window in English.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry period and deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Contest entry period begins at noon ET on Monday, July 7, 2025; final deadline to submit an entry is Wednesday, August 13, 2025 at 5 p.m. ET.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry fees increase by $25 after Monday, August 11, 5 p.m. ET. Submissions must be entered into SABEW’s contest platform no later than the final deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excerpt length and selection
rubrics_metrics.description: Entrants should upload book excerpts with 5,000 words or less.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit an excerpt that showcases the most compelling writing and reporting in the entire work. Do not submit introductory sections that outline the book’s contents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission materials required
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry must include specific materials in the contest platform.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items: an image of the book cover; an image of the table of contents (if it has one); a maximum 5,000-word excerpt; a brief author bio; a short cover letter about the significance of the book’s topic.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and readability of excerpt
rubrics_metrics.description: Uploaded excerpt must be clear and readable and in portrait layout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Book pages should be uploaded in portrait layout, not horizontal/landscape orientation. After submission, SABEW will review the excerpt and ask for another version if the copy is blurry or difficult to read.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finalist physical copies requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: If selected for the final round, entrants must send copies of the complete book to the judging committee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will need to send up to eight copies to the judging committee. All finalists’ books must be printed, including e-books (i.e., provide printed copies even if the work is an e-book).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry fees and member rates
rubrics_metrics.description: $125 entry fee (USD) for nonmembers; $100 entry fee (USD) reduced rate for SABEW members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry fees will increase by $25 after Monday, August 11, 5 p.m. ET. Each category entry requires its own submission and fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Business Reporting — subject matter eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Books in the 'Business Reporting' category must be nonfiction works about companies, business topics, business leaders, markets, economics, or labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category focuses on long-form narrative, history, biography, or analysis. Judges are looking for the quality of the writing and reporting, the craft and power of the storytelling, and the book’s impact and importance within its particular field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Career and Financial Development — subject matter eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Books in the 'Career and Financial Development' category must be nonfiction works offering insight, analysis, or explanation of ideas, strategies, or trends in career development or investing and personal finance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are typically works of service journalism that are useful to individuals, covering topics such as personal productivity, creativity, communication, negotiation, work-life balance, personal growth, career satisfaction, money management, and investment strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category: Management and Leadership — subject matter eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Books in the 'Management and Leadership' category must be nonfiction works about the methods and practice of organizational management and/or corporate leadership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This category includes works that are analytical, instructional, prescriptive, or inspirational. Judges are looking for the quality of the writing and reporting, the originality and persuasiveness of the ideas, and the book’s impact and importance within its particular field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-category submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Books may be submitted in more than one category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each entry requires its own separate submission and entry fee. Example: a book about a legendary investor could be submitted under both 'General Business' and 'Career and Financial Development.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and translation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Books must be written in English or translated into English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The contest is open to publishers internationally as long as the submission is in English and was published in English within the eligibility window. Provide the date the book was published in English if it was translated.

rubrics_metrics.name: ISBN and sales availability
rubrics_metrics.description: All books/e-books must carry an ISBN number and be available for sale in retail/bookstores in North America or internationally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Books that are available by print-on-demand only or online sales only are ineligible. Self-published books are also ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible formats and editions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain types of books are explicitly excluded from entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anthologies, new editions, re-issues, reprints, and collections of previously published work are not eligible, though eligible books may expand on shorter works of published journalism or beat reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges, awards, and committee discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Judging is conducted by a selected panel of business journalists and finance professionals; committee decisions carry certain rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision of the judges as to whether a book is eligible shall be binding. The contest committee reserves the right to give no award in a given category. Winners and finalists will receive a monetary award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality focus for judging (overall evaluative priorities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges prioritize writing/reporting quality, storytelling craft, originality/persuasiveness of ideas, and the book’s impact and importance within its field (as specified per category).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For Business Reporting: 'quality of the writing and reporting, the craft and power of the storytelling, and the book’s impact and importance within its particular field.' For Management and Leadership: 'quality of the writing and reporting, the originality and persuasiveness of the ideas, and the book’s impact and importance.' For Career and Financial Development: usefulness to individuals and clarity/utility of insight, analysis, or explanation.
